ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.

2. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

4. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. happiness
   C. quickly
   D. blue

5. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. goed

6. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

7. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

8. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.

9. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

10. When practising Pronunciation and Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Listening.

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

12. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listenin and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.

3. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

4. A — run

5. B — went

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

10. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Listening.

11. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

12. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listenin; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
